respelling.name: British
respelling.note: Diphthongs and long vowels written with their glide, and the open-mid front vowel as plain e, then the British-only vowels, then the bare weak i and u that Cambridge and Oxford write without a length mark. Digraphs come before their parts so a longer match wins, ɛ becomes e before eə becomes eː, and the bare i and u rows skip what the long-vowel rows already turned into ij and uw.

respelling.name: American
respelling.note: The same glide and open-mid rows as the British group, then every spelling of the rhotic vowel (Cambridge ɝː and ɚ, Longman and Oxford ɜːr, Dictionary.com ɜr) as ər, then the bare i and u most American sources write for FLEECE and GOOSE. The bare rows skip what the long-vowel rows already turned into ij and uw.

note: Language pack for English. Every URL and extraction rule is data — edit here, no recompile. Add a language by creating languages/<Name>/source.json. The 'pronunciation' and 'audio' lists are independent: a site listed for transcriptions need not be listed for recordings, and either list may stand empty. Each list is shown in the order it is written here, whatever order the answers arrive in, so reordering a list reorders the menu. The 'font' block is the typography a headword is drawn in; the 'example' block is the typography example sentences are drawn in; the 'gloss' block is the typography the translations under those example sentences are drawn in, and 'style' may be 'italic' or 'oblique'. Strategies: 'regex' (capture group on body), 'json' (follow dot 'path', then optional 'match'), 'span' (tolerant nested-span IPA reader). 'group' = regex capture group. 'confirm' = regex (with {word}) the body must match. 'normalize' = strip IPA delimiters/entities. 'prefix' = made absolute when the captured address is site-relative. 'varieties' declares the regional varieties this language distinguishes: 'list' rows carry a 'name' and an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 'flag', and 'shown' is 'flag' or 'text' (default 'text') for how the UI labels each reading. A pronunciation attempt may replace its flat extraction keys with a 'readings' list; each row carries the same strategy/match/group/path/normalize keys plus 'variety' (a name from the list, or omitted for untagged) and 'skip' (how many earlier matches to pass over, default 0). All readings run on the same fetched body. A flat attempt without 'readings' is one untagged reading. An audio attempt takes the same 'readings' list, each row capturing one address and tagged with its 'variety'. When the row that opens the audio menu carries no variety, an untagged recording is shown once per declared variety, exactly as an untagged transcription is; when that row already carries a variety, the menu narrows to recordings of that variety alone, an untagged recording collapsing to one row under it. 'respelling' declares ordered regex rewrite groups that recast a looked-up transcription into this pack's preferred symbol convention when the user switches respelling on: each group carries a 'name', a 'varieties' list naming which tagged readings it applies to, and 'rules' as [pattern, replacement] pairs run in written order, each on the previous rule's output; 'cleanup' has the same shape but always runs, for source quirks the built-in dot-and-space removal cannot know. In a pack that declares varieties every group must name the varieties it serves, and a group without a non-empty 'varieties' list is skipped; an untagged reading from a source is shown once per declared variety, each row carrying the same transcription under its own flag. In a pack without varieties 'varieties' may be omitted and untagged readings stay untagged. The respelling switch lives in the Settings panel and is off by default.

pronunciation.name: Longman
pronunciation.note: Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English. The class is upper-case PRON and the reader is case-sensitive. An unknown word returns a results page with no PRON span, so the attempt simply yields nothing.

pronunciation.name: Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The wikitext attempt reads the {{IPA|en|...}} templates and keys each reading on the accent qualifier, |a=RP for British and |a=US or |a=GA for American. The HTML attempt is the untagged fallback.

pronunciation.name: Cambridge
pronunciation.note: Cambridge prints the British transcription inside the <span class="uk dpron-i"> block and the American one inside <span class="us dpron-i">, each as a nested <span class="ipa">. Each reading's match runs from its block's opening tag to the first ipa span, without crossing into the other block.

pronunciation.name: Oxford
pronunciation.note: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries. The headword British transcription is the first <span class="phon"> and the American one the second, so the American reading skips one match; the page 404s on an unknown word, so no confirm guard is needed.

pronunciation.name: Dictionary.com
pronunciation.note: Dictionary.com prints one <span class="txt-ipa"> per variety, each a few hundred characters after a heading that says American or British, and a comma inside one span separates variants of that same variety, sometimes abbreviated with hyphens. Each reading anchors on its heading, allows no other span in between, and takes only the first variant, so a headword without a British section yields American only.

audio.name: Naver
audio.note: Naver English dictionary search API. Each phonetic symbol carries an opaque, token-bearing 'symbolFile' audio URL; the American recording sits under /pron/new/us/ and the British one under /pron/new/uk/, and the first of each in the body belongs to the first entry. The API returns an empty body without a Referer header, so one is declared here.

audio.name: Longman
audio.note: Longman serves the British headword recording under /media/english/breProns/ and the American one under /media/english/ameProns/, both as absolute data-src-mp3 addresses. It appends a cache-busting query to each mp3, which the workspace ignores when it names the saved file.

audio.name: Cambridge
audio.note: Cambridge serves per-entry mp3 audio via site-relative <source type="audio/mpeg"> src attributes; 'prefix' makes them absolute. The British recording sits under /media/english/uk_pron/ and the American one under /media/english/us_pron/, and the first source of each is the headword pronunciation.

audio.name: Oxford
audio.note: Oxford exposes absolute mp3 addresses in data-src-mp3, the British headword recording under /media/english/uk_pron/ and the American one under /media/english/us_pron/.

audio.name: Wiktionary
audio.note: Wiktionary embeds Commons recordings as protocol-relative addresses, so 'prefix' supplies the scheme. Only the transcoded mp3 rendition is taken, because the original is Ogg Vorbis or WAV. The first attempt takes an En- filename, the second a Lingua Libre LL-Q1860_%28eng%29- one, and both prefixes mark the recording as English.
